audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may mix pre-buyout cash flows with a post-buyout common-equity claim
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE anchor and consistency of the parent-common earnings claim
audit_findings.evidence: On March 12, 2025, Emerson completed its purchase of the remaining outstanding shares of common stock of AspenTech not already owned by the Company for approximately $ 7.2 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The March 12, 2025 ownership change is demonstrated: Emerson paid approximately $7.2 billion and eliminated $5.832 billion of noncontrolling interests. A mismatched OE calculation is not demonstrated because the component-level parent/NCI allocation was not supplied. Normalizing to current ownership could increase OE through full AspenTech ownership or decrease it through corrected D&A allocation and associated financing costs; the record cannot establish the net amount or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each FY2025 earnings, D&A, capital-investment and working-capital component between parent and NCI claims, construct full-year current-perimeter AspenTech OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may contain only a partial-year interest burden for the current debt structure
audit_findings.magnitude: computed approximately $107m pretax or $83m after tax annually; approximately $1.73-$2.28 per share of scenario value
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring interest expense reduces equity-level OE directly because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in 2025 reflects higher levels of debt to support the AspenTech transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher burden is demonstrated by $258 million of net interest expense for nine months of FY2026, annualizing to approximately $344 million versus $237 million in FY2025. At the FY2026 22% tax rate, the approximately $107 million pretax difference is about $83 million after tax, or 2.7% of the $3,114.4 million anchor. A proportional rerun lowers the reported scenario values by approximately $1.73-$2.28 per share, far below the $61.31 gap between the $150.21 price and the $88.90 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Replace FY2025 interest with the normalized after-tax cost of June 2026 debt and commercial paper and rerun; do not deduct debt principal separately.

audit_findings.title: AspenTech renewal timing may have temporarily elevated the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $0.15 per diluted share FY2026 nine-month impact; computed approximately $84.4m and approximately $2.06 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary renewal timing enters the FY2025 OE anchor and is then capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Sales for Control Systems & Software increased $270, or 7 percent, reflecting strong growth at AspenTech (including a favorable impact related to the timing of contract renewals) and favorable demand in process and power end markets across all geographies.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing reversal is demonstrated, not merely possible: the FY2026 filing attributes a $0.15-per-share nine-month reduction to software-renewal timing. Using 562.7 million diluted shares gives approximately $84.4 million, or 2.7% of the anchor; applying the valuation's base capitalization factor gives about $2.06 per share. That scale cannot close the $70.20 gap between price and base value and a downward correction reinforces the existing conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the anchor by the documented renewal-timing amount using FY2026 billings and contract balances, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Expiring tax holidays could raise the sustainable cash tax rate
audit_findings.magnitude: computed approximately $22.9m annually for the portion expiring within two years; $38.1m for the entire FY2025 benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher sustainable cash tax rate reduces projected after-tax OE and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately 60 percent of the tax holidays expire over the next two years, with the remainder expiring by 2038.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 filing quantifies the tax-holiday benefit at 1.3 percentage points and says approximately 60% expires within two years. Applying those figures to $2,934 million of FY2025 pretax earnings gives approximately $22.9 million for the near-term expiration and $38.1 million for the entire benefit. Even eliminating the entire benefit corresponds to only about $0.93 per share of base value under the valuation's capitalization factor, versus a $70.20 price-to-base gap.
audit_findings.action: Confirm jurisdictional renewal or replacement expectations and phase out the applicable holiday benefits in projected cash taxes; rerun to document the limited effect.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized software additions may be missing from the maintenance-investment deduction
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back capitalized-software amortization without deducting recurring software additions overstates OE
audit_findings.evidence: Depreciation and amortization includes intellectual property, customer relationships and capitalized software.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $91 million of FY2025 capitalized-software amortization and an $86 million increase in the gross capitalized-software balance, but neither figure establishes cash additions because acquisitions, currency movements, disposals and write-offs may affect the gross balance. The omission itself and its amount therefore remain unresolved, so the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 capitalized-software roll-forward and cash-flow classification, identify recurring additions, deduct them where corresponding amortization was added back, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity value may carry an unrecognized repatriation tax haircut
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $2,180m bridge exposure, or $3.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unavoidable tax or operational restriction reduces the cash and short-term investments added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: No provision has been made for these taxes on approximately $ 5.3 billion of undistributed earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries as of September 30, 2025, as these earnings are considered indefinitely reinvested or otherwise retained for continuing international operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing does not show that the June 2026 cash is trapped, and the $5.3 billion of undistributed foreign earnings is not a cash balance. Nevertheless, even a 100% haircut to the entire $2.180 billion cash bridge removes only $3.80 per share. Bull value would remain approximately $85.10 versus the $150.21 market price, so no possible haircut within the recorded cash balance changes the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map June 2026 cash by jurisdiction and deduct only unavoidable remittance taxes or operationally required cash; no valuation rerun is decision-critical because the maximum bridge effect is bounded.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $86.0m in FY2017; $0 current-anchor effect
audit_findings.mechanism: An eligible residual add-back could raise historical OE and the fitted trend, but the valuation anchors at the lower FY2025 actual
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $86.0m (13.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The unresolved FY2017 residual is $86.0 million, only 13.5% of filed D&A. Adding all of it would raise FY2017 OE from $1,438.2 million to $1,524.2 million, still well below both FY2016 and FY2018. More importantly, the existing $3,350 million trend already exceeds the $3,114.4 million latest-actual anchor; raising an older observation cannot displace the binding MIN(trend, latest) anchor, so the current valuation effect is zero.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2017 residual only for historical completeness; rerun only if the anchoring rule or current-year D&A classification changes.
